about: Text and science values for the filtered-camera monitor screen (eclipse_monitor_screen.gd). English only. The date comes from the NASA fixture, never typed here; Aurora's own timing and view stay labelled as scenario (EX-CH06-S07). The inset is a conceptual diagram of light passing Earth's atmospheric limb; it is not a map and shows no region of Earth (EX-CH06-S07 decision review).

science.ratio_note: Earth (12,742 km across) seen from the Moon at its mean distance of 384,400 km spans about 1.9 degrees; the Sun spans about 0.54 degrees in January (Earth near perihelion), so from the Moon Earth's disc looks about 3.5 times wider than the Sun.
science.ring_note: The rim is sunlight refracted through the lower atmosphere at Earth's edge; Rayleigh scattering removes most blue on the long path, so the light reaching the Moon is red to orange, brightest on the side nearest the hidden Sun.
